title: Nonmembership when the split search fails
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $C,c$ be natural numbers, and let $y$ be a finite binary word. If the bounded search over $0\le n\le |y|$ finds no natural number satisfying $n+(C+1)(n+1)^c=|y|$, then $y$ does not belong to the choice-word verifier language of $N$ with parameters $C,c$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet
No $n$ in the range $0\le n\le |y|$ satisfies $n+(C+1)(n+1)^c=|y|$
replaced: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet and let $C, c$ be natural numbers. If no natural number $n$ satisfies $n + C\,(n+1)^c = |y|$ for a binary string $y$ (so the bounded split search fails at length $|y|$), then $y$ does not belong to the choice-word verifier language of $N$ with parameters $C, c$.
